englishTranslation: Sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots
atAGlance: Xôi xéo is yellow sticky rice with mung bean, usually with fried shallots, chicken fat or oil, and optional toppings.
whatItIs: Xôi xéo is sticky rice topped with shaved mung bean paste, fried shallots, and oil. It is nutty, savory, and especially associated with northern breakfasts.
howToEnjoy: Eat it warm while the mung bean is soft and the fried shallots are crisp. Mix gently so every bite gets rice, bean, and shallot.
howLocalsOrder: Order xôi xéo at morning stalls when you want a northern-style sticky rice packet. Ask for extra fried shallots or pack to go before it is wrapped.
worthKnowing: The name is a Hanoi breakfast signal for many Vietnamese people, even though you can find versions elsewhere.
goodToKnow: Ask for không cay if you want Xôi xéo without added chili.

orderLine.vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần xôi xéo.
orderLine.english: I’d like one order of sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots.
orderLine.pronunciation: chaw toy moht fuhn soy say-oh
